7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Leaving Titus' side, I entered the newly-renovated Drazon Grand Library, its ancient halls now gleaming with fresh polish -- all in preparation for mother's upcoming birthday.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: Under the guise of inspecting the progress, I had arranged for Manus to meet me here, where we could speak freely.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Manus Sazon had requested a private conversation about our final steps, and I used the library's renovation as the perfect excuse to slip away from the prying eyes of the court and guards.

27.speaker: Narrator
27.text: He greeted me immediately, his voice low and careful, as if the very walls might betray us.

31.speaker: Manus Sazon
31.text: "I appreciate you meeting with me here. I didn't want to intrude on the preparations for the Queen Mother's birthday. I know this is a busy time for you."

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: He greeted me immediately with a smile, his voice full of excitement.

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "My declaration of reform has stirred more than just excitement in the kingdom. The nobles are restless, and we need to be ready."

37.speaker: Player_Romus
37.text: "Preparations can wait. What we need to discuss takes priority."

38.speaker: Player_Romus
38.text: "Don't worry about it. It's not as if I could have simply invite you to the Palace."

39.speaker: Player_Romus
39.text: "We don't have much time. Please get to the point."

41.speaker: Manus Sazon
41.text: "The announcement has certainly shaken them, perhaps more than we anticipated."

44.speaker: Manus Sazon
44.text: "Yes, the palace is full of ears these days. The nobles are watching every move we make."

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: He glanced around the library and then shifted his gaze to me.

49.speaker: Manus Sazon
49.text: "Perhaps we should first clarify our direction, Your Majesty..."

50.speaker: Manus Sazon
50.text: "I appreciate the discretion, but the common man doesn't grasp the meaning behind your words."

51.speaker: Manus Sazon
51.text: "But don't worry, Your Majesty. I've been in touch with RPP members and protest leaders, and I can safely say, the declaration has been received with overwhelming support on the ground."

52.speaker: Manus Sazon
52.text: "The reform movement has gained tremendous momentum, and with your backing, it’s more unified than ever."

53.speaker: Manus Sazon
53.text: "The nobles may be restless, but they’re up against a force that’s far stronger and more determined than they realize."

54.speaker: Manus Sazon
54.text: "Among those who believe in the need for reform, there’s a sense of cautious hope."

55.speaker: Manus Sazon
55.text: "After your backing, the movement has gained tremendous momentum. If more people rally behind us, we will have the upper hand in our meeting with the Houses."

60.speaker: Manus Sazon
60.text: "I must say, your support for reforms has shaken the nobility. Perhaps more than we anticipated."

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: He pointed to a stack of documents he was holding.

65.speaker: Manus Sazon
65.text: "But more importantly... I have news, Your Majesty."

66.speaker: Player_Romus
66.text: "I sure hope so, Manus. There is no backing down now."

67.speaker: Player_Romus
67.text: "The nobles won’t go down without a fight. But if we have the people on our side, as you say, it could be our strongest weapon."

68.speaker: Player_Romus
68.text: "That’s reassuring to hear. The nobles have always relied on their influence over the people, believing that their power is unassailable. We will end this soon."

69.speaker: Player_Romus
69.text: "They have no choice but to listen. Or risk losing everything."

70.speaker: Manus Sazon
70.text: "The nobles may be restless, but they’re up against the realities of the modern world. They cannot expect to stand in the way of progress forever."

71.speaker: Player_Romus
71.text: "Of course they can. Not every noble is born in exile to a family with a history of revolting, Manus. You're expecting too much of them."

72.speaker: Manus Sazon
72.text: "The constitution is ready. The RPP and my loyal friends in House Sazon are waiting for us to give the greenlight."

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: He pointed to a stack of documents he was holding.

74.speaker: Manus Sazon
74.text: "The constitution is ready. The RPP and my loyal friends in House Sazon will be waiting for us to give the go ahead."

75.speaker: Player_Romus
75.text: "It was too risky to let my full intentions be known to the nobles. I couldn't compromise myself and my family in that way."

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "I still support the movement, Manus. We'll talk with the Houses, but I don't plan to give them time to act against us."

77.speaker: Manus Sazon
77.text: "The time has come to discuss our final steps."

78.speaker: Manus Sazon
78.text: "Especially with regard to what you were implying in our last conversation."

79.speaker: Manus Sazon
79.text: “We need to ensure their focus is elsewhere if we are to implement these reforms without their knowledge.”

80.speaker: Manus Sazon
80.text: "While there’s no evidence that our plans have been exposed, I can sense the growing suspicion among the royal houses."

81.speaker: Manus Sazon
81.text: "For instance, next month's gathering for the Queen Mother's birthday, where the three royal houses and their most influential leaders will unite to honor her."

82.speaker: Manus Sazon
82.text: "Such an event would be a perfect distraction, but it carries significant risk -- it could either cement our position or expose us."

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "Never mind the risks. The gathering is the perfect setting. We'll let them believe they're in control while we work behind the scenes."

84.speaker: Player_Romus
84.text: "If the royal houses are suspicious, we must act swiftly. We'll use my mother's birthday as a pretext, while making a decisive move behind the scenes to get them in line."

85.speaker: Player_Romus
85.text: "Perhaps we don’t need to do this alone. If the reform movement is as strong as you say, then let’s involve them more directly. We can use the Queen Mother’s birthday as a rallying point -- not just for the nobles, but for the people."
85.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_Movement_Grows"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_DeclareIntention_WeakStatement"] == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_Movement_Grows"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_DeclareIntention_WeakStatement"] == false) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_Movement_Leader_Adarfo"] == true)

89.speaker: Player_Romus
89.text: "I have some reservations about this proposal. That said, if we can feed them false information and steer them down the wrong path, it might erase suspicion and help us pull it off."

90.speaker: Player_Romus
90.text: "I like it. But we’ll need to ensure we don't raise any suspicions.  I'll ensure every detail is meticulously planned."

91.speaker: Player_Romus
91.text: "On second thought, this may not be the right time for drastic action. The Queen Mother’s birthday is too public. A surreptitious approach may be the way to go."

92.speaker: Player_Romus
92.text: "What I meant, Manus, is that we strike during the Queen's birthday and leave nothing to chance. Having them surrounded, we'll present the constitution as our ultimatum."

102.speaker: Player_Romus
102.text: "We make them comply, Manus. They’ll either fall in line, or fall."

103.speaker: Player_Romus
103.text: "They'll do the right thing when they have a gun pointed at their heads."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "If they don’t comply, we eliminate the threat."

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: A look of fear and shock flashed across his face.

107.speaker: Manus Sazon
107.text: "You would... go that far, Your Majesty?"

108.speaker: Player_Romus
108.text: "Leave the details to me, Manus. I'll strike during the celebration and ensure the reforms are carried out."

109.speaker: Manus Sazon
109.text: "Please, Your Majesty. I want reform as much as you do, but I can't condone violent intervention."

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: He looked at me in shock.

111.speaker: Manus Sazon
111.text: "Please, Your Majesty... There is no way for me to do that without telling my relatives about your intentions."

115.speaker: Player_Romus
115.text: "You're worrying too much, Manus. I need you to trust me."

119.speaker: Manus Sazon
119.text: "And what about House Sazon? If you see them as a target, I cannot take part in this."

120.speaker: Manus Sazon
120.text: "My House and my mother will be there too, Your Majesty. I cannot believe you would even suggest something like this."

123.speaker: Manus Sazon
123.text: "What do you mean by a 'decisive move,' Your Majesty?"

124.speaker: Player_Romus
124.text: "Don't worry, Manus. My plan doesn't involve your family. I just need them to cooperate."

125.speaker: Player_Romus
125.text: "You can, Manus. I need House Sazon to support this strike."

126.speaker: Player_Romus
126.text: "If you want this constitution implemented, you *will* listen to me."

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "That's precisely why you will make sure House Sazon stands with us, Manus."

129.speaker: Manus Sazon
129.text: "You know I couldn't do that even if I wanted to."

131.speaker: Player_Romus
131.text: "There isn't. We must do the strike together."

134.speaker: Manus Sazon
134.text: "The reformists will be counting on us."

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "If you want this constitution implemented, you *will* listen to me."

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "Please, Manus. You must listen to me."

138.speaker: Manus Sazon
138.text: "I can’t support this. It’s far too dangerous and aggressive for my liking, Your Majesty."

139.speaker: Manus Sazon
139.text: "We don't need to take any direct measures. Just let the gathering play out without raising any suspicions."

140.speaker: Manus Sazon
140.text: "We can still implement these reforms without their knowledge. You just need to ensure their focus is elsewhere while the House of Delegates does its job."

142.speaker: Player_Romus
142.text: "If you can't do that, then save yourself. Don't attend the gathering and leave this to me."

143.speaker: Manus Sazon
143.text: "But, Your Majesty... You know I can't do that."

147.speaker: Manus Sazon
147.text: "We can still implement these reforms without their knowledge. After all, millions of people are demanding them. You just need to ensure their focus is elsewhere."
147.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_Movement_Grows"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseElections_RPPWinsSeats"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Reform_Movement_Leader_Adarfo"] == true) == false)

149.speaker: Player_Romus
149.text: "Don't worry. We’ll turn the nobles' suspicion into complacency, make them believe they’re still in control while we work behind the scenes."

150.speaker: Player_Romus
150.text: "What if we use the royal houses’ suspicions to our advantage? Let them think they’re on to something. Feed them false information and lead them down the wrong path."

151.speaker: Player_Romus
151.text: "You convinced me, Manus. We'll do it your way."

154.speaker: Manus Sazon
154.text: "Sounds risky. But it could be a clever strategy."

155.speaker: Player_Romus
155.text: "Don't worry. I will ensure we don't raise any suspicions. I will make sure that every detail of the celebration is meticulously planned."

157.speaker: Player_Romus
157.text: "I don't think it will work. I need you to trust me."

158.speaker: Player_Romus
158.text: "Why wouldn't you want a direct solution to these reforms you wanted so badly? Or do you not really care about them as you claim to do?"

159.speaker: Manus Sazon
159.text: "Your Majesty. Violence is not the solution. We can still implement these reforms without the nobility. We have the backing of the people."

160.speaker: Player_Romus
160.text: "If you want this constitution implemented, you *will* listen to me."

161.speaker: Player_Romus
161.text: "I need you to make sure your House is fully behind us and that it doesn't try anything funny. Do you hear me?"

162.speaker: Player_Romus
162.text: "Thank you for everything you've done so far, Manus. But you must leave this final part to me."

163.speaker: Player_Romus
163.text: "I promise you, Manus. Nobody will get hurt. I just need you to trust me on this."

168.speaker: Manus Sazon
168.text: "The people will be counting on you."

169.speaker: Manus Sazon
169.text: "What exactly are you implying? Are you suggesting someone like the Golden Guard be deployed against the other Houses?"

170.speaker: Player_Romus
170.text: "You've heard me, Manus. Please don't make this difficult."

171.speaker: Player_Romus
171.text: "Like I said, you don't need to worry about the details."

172.speaker: Player_Romus
172.text: "Thank you for preparing everything so far, Manus. But let me handle the rest."

173.speaker: Player_Romus
173.text: "I know you warned me against Titus, but I trust him."

174.speaker: Player_Romus
174.text: "I'm sticking to the plan. If you're really afraid to experience how I handle this first-hand, don't attend the gathering. It's up to you."

175.speaker: Manus Sazon
175.text: "The time has come to discuss our final steps. We'll soon have a meeting with the Royal Houses to get their support for our proposal."

176.speaker: Manus Sazon
176.text: "The Queen Mother’s birthday coinciding with the reforms wasn't intentional by any means. However, all three royal houses, along with their most influential leaders, will gather here to pay their respects to Queen Estela..."

177.speaker: Manus Sazon
177.text: "...And use this opportunity to raise their concerns about the proposed reforms."

178.speaker: Manus Sazon
178.text: "We must be willing to compromise when it comes down to it."

185.speaker: Manus Sazon
185.text: "We must remind them about the RPP's legitimate power. We can't let them push us down."

186.speaker: Manus Sazon
186.text: "We must remind them about the massive demands for reform. We can't let them push us down."

188.speaker: Player_Romus
188.text: "Don't worry. I'm confident we'll win them over at the gathering."

189.speaker: Player_Romus
189.text: "I don't think we should push them too far. We should be willing to compromise."

190.speaker: Narrator
190.text: As I looked at him, he immediately extended his hand for a handshake.

192.speaker: Player_Romus
192.text: "Don't you know you must bow before the King when you're introducing yourself?"

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: He inclined his head just the slightest bit forward, not bothering to hide his contempt.

194.speaker: Player_Romus
194.text: "It's a pleasure to properly meet you, Mr. Sotelato. Outside of the zoo that is the House of Delegates, that is."

196.speaker: Narrator
196.text: It hadn't been very long since I'd seen Adarfo at the House of Delegates. Still, the RPP speaker looked even more rugged than I remembered.

197.speaker: Narrator
197.text: Seeing him up close, I noticed the scar that cut across his nose. With his his unkempt beard, and the rugged, olive-green coat -- all of it seemed more fitting for a man of the streets than the polished halls of politics.

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "Good to see you here, House Speaker."

203.speaker: Manus Sazon
203.text: "We were expecting a full declaration of your support for the new constitution to rally the people before we begin talks with the nobility."

204.speaker: Player_Romus
204.text: "I disagree. My support for the reforms was made abundantly clear. How could people not see that?"

205.speaker: Manus Sazon
205.text: "With all due respect, Your Majesty, your announcement was too subtle to stir up too much excitement, but it's still shaken the nobility to some degree."

206.speaker: Player_Romus
206.text: "What's done is done. What do we do now?"

207.speaker: Manus Sazon
207.text: "Among those who believe in the need for reform, there’s still a sense of cautious hope."

212.speaker: Manus Sazon
212.text: "But your declaration certainly did nothing to slow the growing protest movement."

213.speaker: Manus Sazon
213.text: "In any case, we must talk about what we do next."

217.speaker: Manus Sazon
217.text: "I’ll see to it that House Sazon won’t stand in your way."

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: He lowered his head, then suddenly raised it again.

220.speaker: Player_Romus
220.text: "Good. Now get out of here before anyone sees us together."

223.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
223.text: "You'll have to pardon my occasional breach of etiquette. As you can tell, I'm not used to conversing with royalty."

225.speaker: Manus Sazon
225.text: "And we appreciate you meeting with us here, Your Majesty. We really didn't want to intrude on the preparations for the Queen Mother's birthday. I know this is a busy time for you."

229.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
229.text: "The voice of the people has finally grown loud enough to be heard in Palace halls."

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: He smiled. There was something almost disarming about the way he stood -- confident, yet ill-accustomed to the grandeur of our surroundings.

231.speaker: Player_Romus
231.text: "Likewise, Mr. Sotelato. It’s not every day that a Malenyevist and a King have a conversation."

232.speaker: Player_Romus
232.text: "To be frank, I never thought I'd be cooperating with a revolutionary faction. But these are extraordinary times."

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "And is everything faring well with the House of Delegates, Mr. Speaker?"

237.speaker: Player_Romus
237.text: "Good to see you here, Mr. Sotelato."

241.speaker: Narrator
241.text: It hadn't been very long since I'd seen Adarfo at the House of Delegates. Still, the RPP leader looked even more rugged than I remembered.

245.speaker: Player_Romus
245.text: "I hope you are doing something to contain the unrest on the streets, Mr. Sotelato."

246.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
246.text: "What can I say? My fellow RPP members are happy to hear your willingness to work something out with them. But more importantly..."

247.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
247.text: "People expected your full support for the reforms. Your statement did nothing to ease tensions."

254.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
254.text: "Your speech in support of reform helped ease tensions for now. But people are expecting action."

255.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
255.text: "The protests have grown too large to be contained. People are demanding action from the Crown. Now."

256.speaker: Player_Romus
256.text: "It seems that voice has found a formidable mouthpiece in you, Mr. Sotelato."

257.speaker: Player_Romus
257.text: "Don't let that voice get to your head. Don't forget that I'm still your King."

259.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
259.text: "The people’s struggles are my own, Your Majesty. I’ve lived them."

260.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
260.text: "Not in the House of Delegates, not in the streets, and certainly not in Palas Rezna."

261.speaker: Narrator
261.text: Adarfo’s smile faded slightly, replaced by a serious expression.

262.speaker: Narrator
262.text: Adarfo’s smile faded slightly, replaced by a serious expression.

264.speaker: Player_Romus
264.text: "I don't intend for it to be ignored. I want to work together."

265.speaker: Player_Romus
265.text: "The cries of the people may be loud, but governing requires more than just responding to the noise."

266.speaker: Player_Romus
266.text: "I understand your commitment, but you must understand mine as well. My aim is to ensure stability while implementing these reforms."

267.speaker: Player_Romus
267.text: "I don't like your attitude, Mr. Sotelato. I advise you to choose your words carefully."

268.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
268.text: "I won't lie. The change we're demanding will upend stability for a while. Especially for people like you."

269.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
269.text: "That’s why I’m here. I’m willing to work with you, but it must be as equals."

270.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
270.text: "Governing also requires listening, Your Majesty. The cries of the people aren't noise -- they’re a warning."

271.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
271.text: "And I ask of you to consider why my attitude is as it is, Your Majesty. I’m not here to placate or to play politics. I’m here because the people demand change."

272.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
272.text: "I will not betray their trust by tempering my words. We can work together, or we can oppose each other. I will not compromise the truth of what needs to be done.”

273.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
273.text: "But if you don't take decisive action, Your Majesty, the result will be complete and utter chaos."

274.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
274.text: "Despite our differences, I believe we both want what’s best for Rizia."

279.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
279.text: "It's not the nobility you should be concerned about, Your Majesty."

287.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
287.text: "The constitution is ready. The RPP and the reformist coalition are waiting for us to give the greenlight."

291.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
291.text: "The constitution is ready. The RPP and the reformist coalition are waiting for us to give the greenlight."

295.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
295.text: "But more importantly... We have news, Your Majesty."

299.speaker: Narrator
299.text: While Manus looked at me with concern, I noticed a glint in Adarfo's eye.

304.speaker: Narrator
304.text: Manus looked at me with concern, however, there was a noticeable glint in Adarfo's eyes.

308.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
308.text: "I disagree.  A direct strike must be considered. However, I don't support the involvement of Arcasian security forces."

309.speaker: Player_Romus
309.text: "We are here for reforms, not revolution. I advise you to be more respectful with your position towards the Crown."

316.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
316.text: "I also do not support involving the King's personal army with this. But I do think a more decisive approach could be considered."

320.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
320.text: "If we can rally the people behind us, they wouldn't dare oppose it. I believe it's a real possibility."

325.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
325.text: "If they're not willing to be diplomatic..."

326.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
326.text: "I can provide assistance in exploring options regarding such a strike."

327.speaker: Narrator
327.text: Manus looked at us with a defeated expression.

332.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
332.text: "People are already taking to the streets, demanding immediate action from us."

333.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
333.text: "I don't understand why the Crown would even hide its intentions while millions are ready to rally behind us."

334.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
334.text: "The nobility's power is overblown. The real power lies with the people."

335.speaker: Narrator
335.text: Manus took a step closer, his tone firm but measured.

340.speaker: Player_Romus
340.text: "Good. Now I want to speak to Mr. Sotelato alone."

345.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
345.text: "Before I leave, Your Majesty, can I have a one last word with you? I believe our revolutionary compatriots offer the solution you're looking for regarding the strike."

354.speaker: Manus Sazon
354.text: "That can be arranged, but it may scare the Houses even further."

360.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
360.text: "Except on the red lines we've already established and you agreed upon, Your Majesty."

361.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
361.text: "I'm afraid they have no choice but to accept."

364.speaker: Player_Romus
364.text: "That's exactly what I want. To scare them into submission."

365.speaker: Player_Romus
365.text: "Come to think of it, it may not be worth the risk to create such a spectacle. I don't want the talks to turn into chaos."

374.speaker: Player_Romus
374.text: "Are you aware that your radicalism and your red lines are creating obstacles for our reforms?"

375.speaker: Player_Romus
375.text: "I'm afraid your demands made our situation worse. There is a high chance they will not agree to this."

1003.text: "My declaration of reform has stirred more than just excitement in the kingdom. Now that the people are also angry, the nobles will have hard time going against it."

1004.speaker: Player_Romus
1004.text: "You're right, Manus. The momentum is on our side, and we need to act swiftly."

1005.speaker: Player_Romus
1005.text: "Are you certain you have the support of the party now? They were quick to let you go before."

1006.speaker: Player_Romus
1006.text: "Starting the process is one thing; finishing it is another. Do you have the resolve to see this through, even after seeing what happened to Adarfo?"

1008.speaker: Manus Sazon
1008.text: "The new constitution has their support, Your Majesty. I don't need their complete faith in me, only their drive for change."

1009.speaker: Manus Sazon
1009.text: "But for now, they need me as much as I need them. The party understands what's at stake --even if they don't all like it."

1010.speaker: Manus Sazon
1010.text: "I wouldn't have taken this role back if I wasn’t ready to see it through, Your Majesty."

1011.speaker: Manus Sazon
1011.text: "His death doesn't scare me. If I back down now, everything I fought for dies with him. I can’t let that happen."

1012.speaker: Narrator
1012.text: A look of resolve crossed his face.

1016.speaker: Manus Sazon
1016.text: "I must thank you for the Crown's public support to the reform movement."

1021.speaker: Manus Sazon
1021.text: "We should talk about our next steps."

1025.speaker: Titus Gordion
1025.text: "Your new head butler has asked me to inform you that he’s just commissioned a painter for the Queen Mother’s birthday portrait."

1030.speaker: Player_Romus
1030.text: "She must be portrayed as a symbol of strength and valor, embodying the spirit of our victorious forces."

1031.speaker: Player_Romus
1031.text: "Something spiritual and awe-inspiring is the way to go. I want it to bring Wruhecists to their knees."

1034.speaker: Titus Gordion
1034.text: "Though we both know your mother is not an avid sanctuary-goer. I never see her at services."

1038.speaker: Player_Romus
1038.text: "Tell the artist to paint the Queen Mother as she really is."

1040.speaker: Player_Romus
1040.text: "Thank you, Titus. I have settled on a direction."

1041.speaker: Narrator
1041.text: As he stepped back, I glanced toward the library looming ahead, its imposing facade softened by the warm glow of lanterns.

1043.speaker: Player_Romus
1043.text: "I want a portrait depicting Mother as the champion of the common people. The more sympathetic, the better."

1044.speaker: Titus Gordion
1044.text: "Very well, Your Majesty. I'll pass that along."

1049.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
1049.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionDemocratic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMilitaristic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionNormal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionTheocratic"] == true

1050.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
1050.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionDemocratic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionMilitaristic"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionNormal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn09_TalkWithTitus_PortraitTalk_VisionTheocratic"] == true) == false

1051.speaker: Player_Romus
1051.text: "He should make it as regal as possible, befitting the matriarch of House Toras. Perhaps real gold could be used in the paint?"

1053.speaker: Player_Romus
1053.text: "I want something that will appeal to the common people. As if she were not only Queen Mother, but mother to all."

1054.speaker: Titus Gordion
1054.text: "See you soon, Your Majesty. I will be right outside."

1055.speaker: Player_Romus
1055.text: "People should see the portrait and be reminded of the strength and resilience of the Crown."

1056.speaker: Titus Gordion
1056.text: "But, as we both know, your mother is not a Wruhecist."

1057.speaker: Titus Gordion
1057.text: "From what I can tell, Madam Estela distanced herself from her commoner roots long ago."

1058.speaker: Titus Gordion
1058.text: "Such a portrait could appeal to populists, but remind the nobility of the scandal that almost cost your father the Crown."

1059.speaker: Titus Gordion
1059.text: "Yes, that would suit her legacy well, reaffirming House Toras' rule."

1060.speaker: Titus Gordion
1060.text: "Although I would caution against her appearing too high and mighty. You want viewers to feel a connection, not reverence alone."

1074.speaker: Player_Romus
1074.text: "She should be seen as a holy figure. The mother who birthed our great Wruhecist kingdom."

1075.speaker: Player_Romus
1075.text: "We need a fearsome portrayal, one that intimidates and inspires in equal measure."

1076.speaker: Titus Gordion
1076.text: "Any Wruhecist royal would be honored to receive such a portrayal."

1077.speaker: Titus Gordion
1077.text: "She is still the Queen Mother of Rizia. Appropriate tribute must be paid, don't you think?"

1079.speaker: Player_Romus
1079.text: "Let's not do anything too fancy. This is my mother we're talking about."

1080.speaker: Titus Gordion
1080.text: "But of course, you know Madam Estela best."

1081.speaker: Titus Gordion
1081.text: "I like the idea of reinforcing our kingdom's strength through the portrait, Your Majesty."

1082.speaker: Titus Gordion
1082.text: "That said, I find it hard to imagine Madame Estela as much of a warrior."

1092.speaker: Titus Gordion
1092.text: "Mr. Adria asked me to inform you that he’s just commissioned a painter for the Queen Mother’s birthday portrait."

1095.speaker: Titus Gordion
1095.text: "The artist wants to know how Madam Estela should be portrayed."

1096.speaker: Narrator
1096.text: As I was stepping out of the vehicle, Titus cleared his throat, his voice cutting through the evening stillness.

1097.speaker: Narrator
1097.text: Titus drove me to the Drazon Grand Library for me to see how the renovations were shaping up.

1098.speaker: Narrator
1098.text: What he didn’t know, of course, was the real reason for my visit -- to have a private chat with Manus Sazon.

1099.speaker: Narrator
1099.text: I instructed Titus to wait by the car while I inspected the place alone.

1103.speaker: Narrator
1103.text: As Manus was now considered a security threat, we had to be careful to not be seen together. Under the guise of inspecting the progress, I had arranged to meet here, where we could speak freely.

1107.speaker: Player_Romus
1107.text: "I'm sticking to the plan. You are already considered a security threat, so you aren't invited. If you're really so interested in stopping this, come and attend the gathering. It's up to you."

1137.speaker: Titus Gordion
1137.text: "The Queen Mother is 75. I hardly think a festiburu is appropriate."

1138.speaker: Narrator
1138.text: A festiburu was a traditional Rizian festive object filled with treats. Participants took turns striking it until it burst.

1139.speaker: Titus Gordion
1139.text: "Anyway, the portrait's a done deal. Your thoughts?"

1141.speaker: Player_Romus
1141.text: "I haven't decided yet. Would you mind if I ran a few ideas by you?"

1147.speaker: Manus Sazon
1147.text: "When the nobles leave Porte Drazon, we will immediately sign the constitution inside the House of Delegates on live broadcast."

1149.speaker: Player_Romus
1149.text: "I have a bad feeling about this. We've been sneaky so far but I fear we must act swiftly. We'll use my mother's birthday as a pretext, while making a decisive move to get them in line before they can act."

1153.speaker: Manus Sazon
1153.text: "What do you mean by a 'decisive move,' Your Majesty?"

1159.speaker: Narrator
1159.text: Adarfo Sotelato's arrest had sent shockwaves through the country, leaving his followers scrambling to regroup.

1160.speaker: Narrator
1160.text: Manus Sazon had just taken the RPP's leadership again and wanted to talk to me in secret, and I had seized upon the library's renovation as the perfect pretext to slip away from the prying eyes of the court.
